item.title: Heading to Saint Martin’s this week? Here’s how to reach the island
item.description:
Tourists flock to Saint Martin’s Island every year, drawn by its natural beauty. After a long wait, the country’s only coral island is set to reopen to tourists on November 1.
Although tourism activities will resume on the island, ships will not operate during the first five days. Ship services are scheduled to begin on November 6.
This naturally raises a question: how will tourists reach Saint Martin’s Island during these five days?
According to available information, tourists will have to rely on trawlers or speedboats to travel to the island during this period. This means that those planning to visit Saint Martin’s Island between November 1 and 5 will have to use these alternative watercraft.
However, travel by trawler or speedboat will depend heavily on weather conditions, the state of the sea, and permission from the relevant authorities.
This raises several questions. If tourists can travel to the island by trawlers or speedboats, then what is the need for regular ship services?
Travelling by ship may take comparatively longer and cost more. Yet ships hold a different kind of importance for tourists: safety and a relatively stable journey.
For sea travel, larger vessels are generally considered safer and more comfortable than trawlers or smaller speedboats. This is particularly important when the sea is rough, as travelling in smaller vessels can become risky.
So, why will ship services begin five days later?
One of the main reasons is that the vessels concerned have not yet received the necessary clearance from the Department of Environment.
Ship operations are expected to begin on November 6, once the required clearance and other formalities have been completed.
In other words, although the island will reopen to tourists, ship services cannot begin immediately because the approval process is still underway.
Regulating tourism has always been important for protecting the environment and biodiversity of Saint Martin’s Island.
Therefore, before planning a trip, tourists should check the approved modes of transportation, ship schedules, and the latest instructions from the relevant authorities.
Those planning to visit during the first five days should be particularly careful and confirm the safety of travelling by trawler or speedboat, check the weather forecast, and ensure that all necessary permissions are in place before setting out.
The doors to Saint Martin’s Island will reopen on November 1, but tourists will have to wait another five days for regular ship services.
So, before heading to the island, keep in mind not only the travel date but also the mode of transportation and safety arrangements.

item.title: Does charging your phone overnight damage the battery?
item.description:
For many people, putting the phone on charge before bed and unplugging it in the morning is a regular habit. But once the battery hits 100%, many wonder whether keeping it connected to power for hours on end causes damage. With modern smartphones, though, the matter is a little different.
Today’s smartphones usually use lithium-ion or lithium-polymer batteries. Once the phone is fully charged, its charging system reduces the current supplied as needed or shuts off the main charging process. So even after reaching 100%, power does not keep flowing into the battery in the same way. The idea that leaving a phone on charge overnight will “overcharge” and ruin it is therefore not correct.
Even without overcharging, keeping a battery at full charge for a long time is not ideal. In lithium-based batteries, holding a full charge for long periods can gradually speed up chemical degradation. Over time, this affects the battery’s maximum capacity.
As a result, after months or years of use, you may notice the phone’s charge running out faster than before. In other words, the biggest concern with charging overnight is not instant “overcharging,” but a somewhat faster decline in the battery’s health over the long term.
Temperature matters a great deal for batteries. While it is normal for a phone to get a little warm while charging, excessive heat can put extra stress on the battery.
In particular, you should not charge the phone under a pillow, blanket, or bedding. In such places, there is little airflow around the phone, so heat cannot escape easily. It is a safer habit to charge the phone on a hard, flat, open surface.
To help preserve battery life, many smartphones now come with special charging features. Depending on the phone, these may be called Optimized Charging, Adaptive Charging, or Battery Protection.
These features analyze the user’s charging habits and often avoid holding the phone at 100% for long, instead completing the full charge closer to a set time. This reduces the amount of time the battery spends fully charged.
So, is it fine to sleep with the phone on charge?
Because modern smartphones have multiple safeguards that control charging, leaving the phone plugged in overnight generally won’t cause immediate damage. However, to keep the battery healthy in the long run, it is best to avoid overheating and keep features such as Optimized Charging or Battery Protection enabled.
Remember, a smartphone battery is a consumable component. Even with good care, its capacity will decline over time. The idea that a battery is ruined only because of overnight charging is not correct. Rather, temperature, usage patterns, and the age of the battery all combine to determine how long it lasts.

item.title: Try these five tricks to stop overpaying for your AC
item.description:
As temperatures continue to rise, staying comfortable indoors has become increasingly difficult. From ceiling fans and air coolers to air conditioners, people are relying on different cooling solutions to cope with the heat. However, running an air conditioner for extended periods can raise concerns about electricity costs, particularly among middle-income households.
Many people limit their use of air conditioners at night to avoid high electricity bills, often compromising their comfort in the process. However, with a few adjustments to everyday habits, it is possible to maintain a comfortable indoor temperature while managing energy consumption.
Here are some practical ways to make your air conditioner more energy-efficient.
The temperature setting plays an important role in determining how much electricity an air conditioner consumes. Lower settings require the compressor to work harder and for longer periods, increasing energy use.
According to a recent study cited in the original report, each degree of reduction in the temperature setting can increase electricity consumption by around 6%. Keeping the thermostat at a moderate temperature, therefore, can help reduce unnecessary energy use.
Setting the air conditioner to 18°C may seem like an effective way to cool a room quickly, but it can significantly increase energy consumption. A setting of 24°C is generally sufficient to maintain a comfortable indoor environment during hot weather.
Instead of lowering the temperature excessively, gradually adjust your nighttime settings to 24°C. This can help maintain comfort while reducing the strain on the air conditioner's cooling system.
An air conditioner works more efficiently when cool air remains inside the room. Open doors, poorly sealed windows, and gaps around frames allow cool air to escape while letting warm air enter.
Make sure all doors and windows are properly closed before switching on the AC. Check for gaps that may need sealing and use curtains to reduce heat entering through windows.
Electronic appliances generate heat while operating, which can increase the cooling load on an air conditioner. Televisions, computers, and other devices can contribute to indoor heat, making the AC work harder to maintain the desired temperature.
Switch off appliances that are not in use before going to bed. This can help reduce unnecessary heat generation and improve cooling efficiency.
Running an air conditioner throughout the night may not always be necessary. As the room cools down, maintaining the same level of cooling until morning can lead to unnecessary electricity consumption.
Use the timer function to schedule the AC to switch off one or two hours before your usual wake-up time, if the room remains comfortable. This can help avoid excessive cooling and reduce operating time.
With the right temperature settings, proper room insulation, and mindful use of household appliances, you can enjoy a cooler night's sleep without putting unnecessary pressure on your electricity bill.

item.title: Hakimi bags hat-trick as PSG rip Le Havre to pieces
item.description:
Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.
PSG's nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice dropping four points adrift while Olivier Giroud's late goal lifted Lille second after their 1-0 home win over Lens.
The former World Cup and Champions League winner Giroud is now 40 and the giant striker was flushed red with pleasure after his 86th minute shot settled a tense, tight struggle.
PSG top the table with 20 points after nine games, Lille are second on 18, Monaco can join them should they beat Paris FC on Sunday, while Rennes have 16.
On just two points so far Le Havre gave PSG a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.
Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi through-ball to level on 26 minutes.
Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.
The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the 'keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.
On a lightning break the hosts poured everyone forward in a brave but naive effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half.
Senny Mayulu ran around the horrified stopper, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net with nobody in the box effectively ending the contest, just after the hour.
Hakimi's hat-trick arrived when he threaded a shot through a forest of players on 69 minutes and had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.
"He's a striker when we have the ball. He's free to do that when we are in possession, but obliged to defend when we aren't," said Luis Enrique.
The Spanish coach left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench while Ousmane Dembele and Georgian attacker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were missing through injury.
